definition: A small holder or butterfly of yarn for one color area in C2C or intarsia work.
Chain space; see Chain space.
See Foundation stitches.
Double crochet two together, a one-stitch decrease (UK: tr2tog).
A narrow decorative border worked along an edge.
Shrinking and matting animal-fiber fabric with heat, moisture and agitation.
A sample worked to measure gauge; see Swatch.
Yarn wound in a large loop and twisted; wind it into a ball before use.
To connect the end of a round to its beginning (usually with a sl st), or to connect pieces.
The working loop on the hook; never counted as a stitch.
A sewn seam worked from the right side that is nearly invisible.
One of the strands twisted together to make a yarn.
A section of instructions or chart worked more than once.
Stretchy fabric of alternating raised and recessed columns or ridges, used for bands and cuffs.
Single crochet two together, a one-stitch decrease (UK: dc2tog).
A small freeform patch of mixed stitches and textures.
Partial rows worked to add depth in one area of a piece.
Wool treated to resist felting so it can be machine washed.
The cut end of the yarn at the start or end of work.
A reviewer who checks a pattern's math, consistency and clarity.
Yarn dyed with several colors along its length.
A simple overcast sewn seam.
The length of yarn in a ball or needed for a project.
Small stuffed crocheted toys or figures, usually worked in tight single crochet spirals.
The horizontal bar behind the top V of a stitch (especially hdc); also the bump on the back of a chain.
The loop of the top V farthest from you.
Wetting, steaming or spraying finished crochet and pinning it to shape to dry.
A group of incomplete tall stitches worked in one stitch and closed together so they pop out of the fabric.
Rounds or rows worked around the outside of a finished piece.
Lace made from a narrow crocheted tape that is turned and joined to itself.
The gap under one or more chains, worked into rather than into the chains themselves.
A drawing of a pattern using symbols (stitch chart) or colored squares (color chart).
Several partial stitches worked into one or more stitches and finished together at the top.
Any technique that places colors in a pattern: stripes, tapestry, mosaic, C2C, intarsia.
A method built from small diagonal tiles, often used for pixel pictures.
Reverse single crochet, worked in the opposite direction to give a corded edge.
Reducing the stitch count, usually by working stitches together.
How a fabric hangs and flows.
A batch of yarn dyed together; lots can differ slightly in color.
The difference between a body measurement and the finished garment measurement. Negative ease means the item is smaller than the body.
Cut the yarn and pull the tail through the last loop to secure it.
A mesh of open and filled squares that forms pictures or letters.
Strands of unused color carried across the back of the work (in crochet, usually hidden inside stitches instead).
The chain that starts a piece worked in rows.
Stitches that create the chain and first row at the same time (fsc, fdc).
Pulling out stitches to undo work (rip-it, rip-it).
The loop of the top V nearest to you.
The number of stitches and rows in a measured area; UK: tension.
A square motif worked in rounds of clusters, traditionally three dc, separated by chain spaces.
Lace strips made on a two-pronged loom with a crochet hook.
Adding stitches, usually by working more than one stitch into the same place.
Colorwork with separate yarn sections for each color block, not carried across.
A front-loops decrease used in amigurumi to hide decreases.
Finishing a round by sewing the tail through the next stitch to imitate a stitch top.
Lace made of separately worked dimensional motifs joined by a mesh background.
An adjustable loop that lets the center of a round piece close completely; also magic circle.
Colorwork worked one color per row, using dropped stitches into lower rows to place color.
A single shaped unit (square, hexagon, flower) that is joined to others.
A finished measurement smaller than the body measurement, so the item stretches to fit.
A small chain loop, closed with a slip stitch, used as a decorative bump.
A group of complete stitches closed together by drawing a loop through the first stitch.
The vertical body of a stitch.
Several loops drawn up in one stitch and closed together.
The side of the fabric meant to be seen.
A circuit of stitches worked around a center or tube.
A line of stitches worked back and forth; the work is turned at each end.
Several stitches worked into the same stitch or space, fanning outward.
A twisted or wound package of yarn; also ball, hank, cake.
An adjustable knot that puts the first loop on the hook.
A stitch worked into a row below the current one, leaving a long stem.
Rounds worked continuously without joining; common in amigurumi.
A removable clip or ring placed in a stitch to mark a position.
The number of stitches needed for one repeat of a pattern, often with extras for edges (e.g., multiple of 6 + 2).
A test piece used to measure gauge and preview fabric.
Colorwork in which unused colors are carried inside the stitches.
How tightly you hold the yarn; UK patterns also use tension to mean gauge.
The two loops at the top of a stitch, shaped like a sideways V.
A crochet method in which loops are collected on a long hook in a forward pass and worked off in a return pass.
Chains made at the start of a row to raise the hook to the height of the stitches.
Securing yarn tails by threading them through stitches on the wrong side.
The yarn coming from the ball, as opposed to the tail.
The number of times a yarn wraps side by side in an inch; used to estimate weight.
The side not meant to be seen.
Wrapping the yarn over the hook from back to front; UK: yarn round hook.
